name: The Imperial Library — Developer and Obscure Texts

rules: Preserve exact author/speaker, original venue, date when known, archive/republication location, and whether the author was a developer at the time.
Developer statements are not automatically in-game canon and never silently override contradictory primary game evidence.
Obscure texts authored by developers are stored as their own evidence class, distinct from in-game books, dialogue, quest events, manuals, and official marketing/lore publications.
Posts, interviews, roleplay statements, forum answers, design documents, drafts, and fiction are separate document kinds.
Later incorporation of an idea into a released game creates a new primary-source evidence link; it does not retroactively turn the earlier text into primary evidence.
Preserve contradictions and revisions across authors and dates instead of synthesizing a single hidden canon.
Fan questions and surrounding discussion must be separable from developer-authored answers.
Claims derived from archived copies retain original-source provenance plus archive provenance.

notes: This collection begins a dedicated Imperial Library ingestion stream.
Article bodies remain local derived corpus data; Git stores manifests, provenance, durable extracted records and crawl state.
